title: Stable formulas and definability of types over models
summary: Use finite rows of a stable formula to define each local type over a model, bound their number, and distinguish definition from realization.
abstract: An element in a larger structure can answer infinitely many questions involving parameters from a smaller model. Stability puts a finite description on the answers made by one fixed formula: finitely many rows already distinguish every positive parameter test from every negative one. Combining those rows gives a formula that defines the entire answer set using parameters from the original model. This bounds the number of such descriptions over an infinite model by the model's own size, even when the language is large. Equality supplies a useful distinction: the description of a point unequal to every named element has a simple definition, although no point of the original model realizes it.
